title: Approvals
description:
Approvals: the shapes the agent worker, the approval store in the realtime server, the browser's approval card, OUI's surface runtime and a conversation engine exchange. An irreversible action — a `transaction`, or a `write` declared `destructive` — runs only on an approval the person gave, bound to the exact call by a single-use token.

1. The worker stops the turn at the call and stores it (`PendingApprovalInput`); the person's tab receives `agent:approval_required` (`ApprovalRequiredEvent`) and renders the approval card from its `preview`, whose every word comes from the action's declaration, never from the model.
2. In a UI only a click on the card counts: the card sends `approval:decide` (`ApprovalDecidePayload`) from the person's own socket. On a conversation channel, the verbatim `readback` and an affirmative next turn. An action on the person's page is approved by its card, or on `voice`, `phone` and `chat` by its readback and an affirmative next turn: the store then pushes the tab a single-use grant (`ApprovalGrantedEvent`), which one tab claims (`ApprovalClaimPayload`, `ApprovalClaimResult`).
3. The store answers the decider only (`ApprovalDecideResult`): a single-use token, a compact JWS (`ApprovalTokenClaims`), and the call's `argsHash`. The tab's OUI runtime holds an `ApprovalGrant`: from the click's answer, or from the claimed push.
4. The next turn carries the token (`ApprovalContinuation`); the worker redeems it for the stored call, exactly (`ApprovedCall`), and runs it. A UI action request then carries `approval` (`ActionRequestApproval`), which the browser checks against its grant before it runs the handler.
5. When the realtime server holds receipt keys, redemption also returns a receipt (`ApprovalReceiptClaims`): a compact JWS, EdDSA over Ed25519, that the approved host or API call carries to the tool's own API (the `OUI-Approval-Receipt` header). The tool verifies it offline against the realtime server's published keys (`/.well-known/oui-approval-jwks.json`); a UI action gets none.

The args hash is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the call's arguments, lowercase hex; `oui-spec/approval-vectors.json` holds every implementation, in any language, to it.

ArgsHash.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of a call's arguments, lowercase hex.

ApprovalChannel.description: Where the person confirmed. In a UI only a click on the card counts (`ui`); in a conversation channel, the verbatim readback and an affirmative next turn. An action on the person's page is approved by its card, or on `voice`, `phone` and `chat` (`READBACK_UI_APPROVAL_CHANNELS`) by its readback; never by SMS.

ApprovalPreviewArgument.description: One argument of the call, as the person reads it: its declared label and its value in words.

name.description: The argument's name in the call.

label.description: Its label, from the action's input schema.

ApprovalPreview.description: What the person is asked to approve. By default every word comes from the action's declaration (its title, description and input schema labels), never from the model. A host may write this display copy itself (the worker's `approvals.preview`), to redact a value or to speak the person's language: the call that runs, and the args hash it is bound to, stay the original.

consequence.description: What running it does, from the declaration.

readback.description: One sentence composed from the fields above, read or sent verbatim on a conversation channel.

spokenReadback.description: The readback as a voice should say it, when the host wrote one: dates, times and numbers in words, digits grouped for speech. A voice channel speaks it in place of `readback`; every other channel uses `readback`.

ApprovalEffect.description: The effect the approval is for: the action's declared effect kind (`transaction` for an irreversible external act), or `write` when it declares none.

PendingApprovalInput.description: A call waiting for the person's approval, as the worker stores it (`POST /internal/approvals`).

userId.description: The user whose turn made the call: the only one who may decide it.

accountId.description: The user's account, when the product has one: carried on the call's receipt.

toolKind.description: `ui` for an action on the person's page, which gets no receipt (the browser checks its own grant); `backend` for a host or API tool. Absent is `backend`.

room.description: For an action on the person's page: the realtime room of the turn that asked (its `socketRoom`), where the action is dispatched. When the person approves it by voice or in chat, its grant is pushed to this room and nowhere else. Never set on a host or API tool.

operationId.description: For a generated API tool, its OpenAPI `operationId`: carried on the call's receipt.

audience.description: The API the call's receipt is for, fixed when the approval is created: the origin (scheme, host and port) the tool calls. For a generated API tool, its operation's server URL's origin; for a host tool, its declared `approvalAudience`. Absent on a host tool that names none: the realtime server's default audience, the product's own origin, is used. Never set on a UI action.

argsSensitive.description: Whether the arguments may be written to logs. They are only when the declaration says they are not sensitive.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms, at most 30 minutes away (`MAX_APPROVAL_TTL_MS`).

ApprovalRequiredEvent.description: `agent:approval_required`: the worker stopped the turn at a call that needs the person's approval. The approval card renders it.

ApprovalDecidePayload.description: `approval:decide`, from the person's own socket: the card's click.

ApprovalRefusalReason.description:
Why an approval was refused:

- `unknown`: no such pending approval, or grant: never stored, already declined or redeemed, withdrawn, or expired and gone.
- `forbidden`: another user's approval, or another conversation's; or a grant claimed from a socket that is not in its room.
- `expired`.
- `decided`: already decided.
- `used`: already redeemed; or a grant another tab has claimed.
- `invalid`: not a token this environment signed, or malformed.
- `mismatch`: signed, but not for the stored call.
- `channel`: a decision from a channel that may not make it: an action on the person's page approved by SMS, or by voice or chat when no room was stored with it.

ApprovalDecideResult.description: The answer to a decision. An approval's token goes only to the decider: the socket that clicked, or the engine that asked.

token.description: The single-use token the continuation turn redeems.

argsHash.description: What the browser checks a UI action's params against before it runs it.

ApprovalGrantedEvent.description: `agent:approval_granted`: the person approved an action on their page by voice, on the phone or in chat, after its verbatim readback. The approval store pushes it, in the same step as the decision, to the room stored with the approval and nowhere else; the realtime server's emit API refuses it. A tab whose open conversation is `conversationId` and which is joined to `room` claims it (`approval:claim`); only the first claim is answered with the grant.

grantId.description: This grant, single use: what a claim names.

argsHash.description: The approved call's args hash: what the tab's OUI runtime checks the request's params against.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms: two minutes after the decision (`APPROVAL_GRANT_TTL_MS`), or the approval's own expiry if sooner. A claim after it is refused, and the runtime admits nothing after it.

room.description: The room it was pushed to: that of the turn that asked.

ReadbackUIApprovalChannel.description: The conversation channels on which an action on the person's page is approved by its readback and an affirmative next turn, as well as by its card.

ApprovalDeclinedEvent.description: `agent:approval_declined`: the person declined an action on their page in a conversation channel. Pushed by the approval store to the room stored with the approval, so the card on screen says so. The emit API refuses it.

channel.description: Where the person declined it: a conversation channel.

ApprovalClaimPayload.description: `approval:claim`, from the person's own socket: this tab takes the pushed grant. The store answers only the first claim, from a socket of the approval's user that is in the grant's room, before the grant expires.

ApprovalClaimResult.description: The answer to a claim: the grant, for this tab's OUI runtime (`runtime.grantApproval`), with where the person approved it; or why not. Only one claim of a grant is ever answered with it.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which the grant no longer admits anything.

ApprovalTokenClaims.description: The token's claims: a compact JWS (HS256), signed with the environment's approval key.

aid.description: The approval id, which is the tool call id.

ApprovalReceiptClaims.description: An approval receipt's claims: a compact JWS whose header is `{ "alg": "EdDSA", "typ": "oui-approval-receipt+jwt", "kid" }`, signed by the realtime server with an Ed25519 key only it holds, when it redeems a token. It says this user approved exactly this call, in this conversation, and the approval was redeemed just now. A tool verifies it with the server's public keys (`verifyApprovalReceipt` in `@ouispec/agent-core`, or any JOSE library), refuses it once expired, and acts on each `jti` at most once.

iss.description: The realtime server's public base URL. Its keys are published at `<iss>/.well-known/oui-approval-jwks.json`.

aud.description: The one API the receipt is for: an origin, fixed when the approval was created. Another API refuses it.

approvalId.description: The approval id, which is the tool call id.

argsHash.description: The approved call's args hash. The tool computes it from the request it received and compares.

tool.description: The tool's name, as the worker offered it.

operationId.description: For a generated API tool, its OpenAPI `operationId`.

accountId.description: The user's account, when the product has one.

jti.description: Unique to this receipt: the call's idempotency key. A tool acts on each at most once.

ApprovedCall.description: What redeeming a token returns: the stored call, exactly, for the worker to run.

receipt.description: The receipt for this call (`ApprovalReceiptClaims`), when the realtime server holds receipt keys and the call is a host or API tool's. The worker hands it to the tool as `ctx.approval.receipt`.

ApprovalStatus.description: An approval's state, for the turn that follows a decision.

ApprovalContinuation.description: What a turn that follows a decision carries, outside the message text: the token to redeem, or that the person declined.

ActionRequestApproval.description: What a UI action request carries when it runs an approved call (`OUIActionApproval`): the browser runs a `transaction` or destructive action only when this matches a grant this tab received from its own card click, or claimed from the push of an approval given by voice or in chat.

argsHash.description: `argsHash(params)` of the request the user approved.

ApprovalGrant.description: What this tab's OUI runtime holds (`runtime.grantApproval`, `OUIApprovalGrant`): the request the person approved, from their click on the card or from a claimed push, until it expires.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which the grant no longer admits anything.
